sources.title: Notes on Diffy Qs: Differential Equations for Engineers

concepts.name: Differential equation
concepts.statement: A differential equation is an equation that involves not only an unknown variable, but also its derivatives.

concepts.name: Dependent variable
concepts.statement: The dependent variable is the unknown of a differential equation, a function of the independent variable; solving the equation means finding it.

concepts.name: Independent variable
concepts.statement: The independent variable is the variable the unknown of a differential equation is a function of, such as t in dx/dt + x = 2 cos t.

concepts.name: First-order differential equation
concepts.statement: A first-order differential equation involves only the first derivative of the dependent variable; the general form is dy/dx = f(x, y).

concepts.name: Solution of a differential equation
concepts.statement: A solution of a differential equation is a function of the independent variable that makes the equation hold, left-hand side equal to right-hand side, when it and its derivatives are plugged in. An equation may have many solutions.

concepts.name: Checking a solution
concepts.statement: Computing the derivatives of a proposed function and plugging them into the equation to see whether the two sides agree; it is how a remembered or guessed solution is confirmed.

concepts.name: Ordinary differential equation
concepts.statement: An ordinary differential equation (ODE) is an equation where the derivatives are taken with respect to only one variable, so there is only one independent variable.

concepts.name: Partial differential equation
concepts.statement: A partial differential equation (PDE) is an equation that depends on partial derivatives with respect to several independent variables.

concepts.name: Real-world problem
concepts.statement: The situation in science or engineering that a differential equation is used to understand, the start and the end of the modelling cycle.

concepts.name: Mathematical model
concepts.statement: The differential equation (or equations) a real-world problem is translated into, after simplifying assumptions are made.

concepts.name: Mathematical solution
concepts.statement: The solution mathematics gives for a mathematical model, which must still be interpreted to say what it means for the real-world problem.

concepts.name: Exponential growth model
concepts.statement: The exponential growth model says that a population grows at a rate proportional to itself, dP/dt = kP for a constant k > 0; its solutions are P(t) = Ce^(kt).

concepts.name: Initial condition
concepts.statement: An initial condition gives the value of the solution at one point, such as P(0) = 1000; it picks out the constant in the general solution.

concepts.name: General solution
concepts.statement: The general solution is a formula with constants, such as P(t) = Ce^t, in which every solution of the equation can be written for some choice of the constants.

concepts.name: Particular solution
concepts.statement: A particular solution is the one solution sought, found from the general solution by an initial condition; generally, any one solution.

concepts.name: Solving for the constants
concepts.statement: Plugging the initial conditions into the general solution and solving for its constants, one condition for each constant, to get the particular solution.

concepts.name: Four fundamental equations
concepts.statement: Four equations whose solutions are worth memorizing, for a constant k > 0: dy/dx = ky has y = Ce^(kx); dy/dx = −ky has y = Ce^(−kx); y″ = −k²y has y = C₁ cos(kx) + C₂ sin(kx); y″ = k²y has y = C₁e^(kx) + C₂e^(−kx), or D₁ cosh(kx) + D₂ sinh(kx).

concepts.name: Second-order differential equation
concepts.statement: A second-order differential equation involves the second derivative of the dependent variable and no higher; its general solution has two constants.

concepts.name: Hyperbolic functions
concepts.statement: The hyperbolic cosine and hyperbolic sine are cosh x = (eˣ + e⁻ˣ)/2 and sinh x = (eˣ − e⁻ˣ)/2, with cosh 0 = 1 and sinh 0 = 0.

concepts.name: Derivatives of the hyperbolic functions
concepts.statement: The derivative of cosh x is sinh x, with no minus sign, and the derivative of sinh x is cosh x.

concepts.name: Catenary
concepts.statement: The catenary is the shape of a hanging chain, the graph of cosh; inverted, it is the ideal arch for supporting its own weight, which a parabola is not.

forms.condition: the Gateway Arch in Saint Louis, A = 68.7672, C = 3.0022, L = 299.2239

concepts.name: System of differential equations
concepts.statement: Several differential equations working together, such as y′ = x, x′ = y, form a system of differential equations.

concepts.name: Order of a differential equation
concepts.statement: The order of an equation or system is the order of the largest derivative that appears in it.

concepts.name: Linear equation
concepts.statement: An equation is linear if the dependent variable (or variables) and their derivatives appear only as first powers, are not multiplied together, and no other functions of them appear; a linear ODE can be put in the form (2).

forms.latex: a_n(x) \frac{d^n y}{dx^n} + a_{n-1}(x) \frac{d^{n-1} y}{dx^{n-1}} + \cdots + a_{1}(x) \frac{dy}{dx} + a_{0}(x) y = b(x)

concepts.name: Coefficients
concepts.statement: The coefficients of a linear equation are the functions a₀, a₁, …, aₙ that multiply the dependent variable or one of its derivatives, not the function b(x) standing alone.

concepts.name: Nonlinear equation
concepts.statement: An equation that is not linear is nonlinear, such as dx/dt = x² or the pendulum equation θ″ + sin θ = 0.

concepts.name: Homogeneous equation
concepts.statement: A linear equation is homogeneous if every term depends on the dependent variable, so no term is a function of the independent variables alone.

forms.latex: a_n(x) \frac{d^n y}{dx^n} + a_{n-1}(x) \frac{d^{n-1} y}{dx^{n-1}} + \cdots + a_{1}(x) \frac{dy}{dx} + a_{0}(x) y = 0

concepts.name: Nonhomogeneous equation
concepts.statement: A linear equation with a term that is a function of the independent variables alone, such as b(x) in (2) when b is not zero, is nonhomogeneous, or inhomogeneous.

concepts.name: Constant coefficients
concepts.statement: A linear equation has constant coefficients if its coefficients are constant functions; the function b standing alone may still depend on the independent variable.

forms.latex: a_n \frac{d^n y}{dx^n} + a_{n-1} \frac{d^{n-1} y}{dx^{n-1}} + \cdots + a_{1} \frac{dy}{dx} + a_{0} y = b(x)

concepts.name: Variable-coefficient equation
concepts.statement: A linear equation whose coefficients are not constants is a variable-coefficient equation.

concepts.name: Autonomous equation
concepts.statement: An equation or system is autonomous if it does not depend on the independent variable, which is then thought of as time; a first-order autonomous ODE has the form dx/dt = f(x).

concepts.name: Antiderivative
concepts.statement: An antiderivative of f(x) is a function whose derivative is f(x); the indefinite integral ∫f(x) dx + C is really the whole one-parameter family of antiderivatives, and to integrate, here, means to antidifferentiate.

concepts.name: Closed form
concepts.statement: A closed form is a formula in terms of known functions with no integrals or limits.

concepts.name: Solution by integration
concepts.statement: The equation y′ = f(x) is solved by integrating: its general solution is y(x) = ∫f(x) dx + C, and the solution with y(x₀) = y₀ is the definite integral y(x) = ∫ from x₀ to x of f(t) dt + y₀, which exists wherever f is continuous and can be computed even when no closed form exists.

concepts.name: Switching the roles of x and y
concepts.statement: An equation y′ = f(y) is solved by treating x as a function of y: dx/dy = 1/f(y), so x(y) = ∫ 1/f(y) dy + C, which is then solved for y; constant solutions where f(y) = 0 are found separately.

concepts.name: Slope field
concepts.statement: The slope field of y′ = f(x, y) is the picture of short lines drawn at a grid of points (x, y), each with the slope f(x, y), which is the slope a solution through that point must have; solutions are curves that follow the slopes.

concepts.name: Picard’s theorem on existence and uniqueness
concepts.statement: If f(x, y) is continuous and ∂f/∂y exists and is continuous near (x₀, y₀), then a solution to y′ = f(x, y), y(x₀) = y₀, exists, at least for x in some small interval, and is unique.

concepts.name: Separable equation
concepts.statement: A differential equation is separable if it can be written as y′ = f(x)g(y) for some functions f(x) and g(y).

concepts.name: Separating variables
concepts.statement: A separable equation dy/dx = f(x)g(y) is solved by separating the variables, dy/g(y) = f(x) dx, and integrating both sides, ∫ dy/g(y) = ∫ f(x) dx + C, then solving for y if possible; the solutions where g(y) = 0 are checked separately.

concepts.name: Implicit solution
concepts.statement: An implicit solution is a solution left as an equation relating x and y, such as y² + 2 ln|y| = x² + D, when it is hard to solve for y explicitly; it is checked by implicit differentiation.

concepts.name: Singular solution
concepts.statement: A singular solution is an extra solution that comes up due to division by zero while separating variables, such as y = 0 for y′ = xy/(y² + 1); it is often not given by any value of the constant in the general formula.

concepts.name: Newton’s law of cooling
concepts.statement: The rate at which the temperature T of an object changes is proportional to the difference between the ambient temperature A and T: dT/dt = k(A − T) for some positive constant k.

concepts.name: First-order linear equation
concepts.statement: A first-order equation is linear if it can be put in the form y′ + p(x)y = f(x): it is linear in y and y′, with no higher powers or functions of them, while the dependence on x can be more complicated.

concepts.name: Integrating factor
concepts.statement: The integrating factor of y′ + p(x)y = f(x) is the function r(x) = e^(∫p(x) dx), chosen so that r(x)y′ + r(x)p(x)y is the derivative of the product r(x)y; any antiderivative of p will do.

concepts.name: Integrating factor method
concepts.statement: To solve y′ + p(x)y = f(x), multiply by the integrating factor r(x) = e^(∫p dx) so the left side becomes d/dx[r(x)y], integrate both sides, and divide by r(x): y = e^(−∫p dx)(∫e^(∫p dx)f(x) dx + C). It is easier to remember the process than the formula.

forms.latex: y = e^{-\int p(x) \,dx} \left( \int e^{\int p(x) \,dx} f(x) \,dx + C \right)

concepts.name: Solution of the linear initial value problem
concepts.statement: The solution of y′ + p(x)y = f(x), y(x₀) = y₀, written with definite integrals and careful dummy variables, is the boxed formula (1.4), which a computer or calculator can evaluate.

forms.latex: y(x) = e^{-\int_{x_0}^x p(s)\, ds} \left( \int_{x_0}^x e^{\int_{x_0}^t p(s)\, ds} f(t) \,dt + y_0 \right)

concepts.name: Existence for linear equations
concepts.statement: If p(x) and f(x) are continuous on an interval (a, b), the solution y(x) of y′ + p(x)y = f(x), y(x₀) = y₀, exists and is differentiable on all of (a, b), unlike the solution of a nonlinear equation such as y′ = y².

concepts.name: Setting up a mixing problem
concepts.statement: For a well-stirred tank, the amount x of a dissolved substance changes at the rate in times the concentration in, minus the rate out times the concentration out, where the concentration out is x divided by the current volume; the result is a first-order linear equation.

concepts.name: Solving by substitution
concepts.statement: An equation that is neither separable nor linear may become one after a change of variables: a new dependent variable v, a function of x, is chosen (often the most complicated part of the equation), y′ is written in terms of v′, v and x, the new equation is solved, and the result is unsubstituted.

concepts.name: Bernoulli equation
concepts.statement: A Bernoulli equation is an equation of the form y′ + p(x)y = q(x)yⁿ; for n = 0 or n = 1 it is linear, and n need not be an integer.

concepts.name: Bernoulli’s substitution
concepts.statement: For n ≠ 0, 1, the substitution v = y^(1−n) transforms the Bernoulli equation into the linear equation v′ + (1 − n)p(x)v = (1 − n)q(x).

concepts.name: Homogeneous first-order equation
concepts.statement: A homogeneous equation, in the sense of substitution, is a first-order equation that can be written as y′ = F(y/x).

concepts.name: Solution of a homogeneous equation
concepts.statement: The substitution v = y/x, so that y′ = v + xv′, turns y′ = F(y/x) into the separable equation xv′ = F(v) − v, with the implicit solution ∫ dv/(F(v) − v) = ln|x| + C, for x > 0 or x < 0 as the initial condition decides.

concepts.name: Equilibrium solution
concepts.statement: An equilibrium solution of an autonomous equation dx/dt = f(x) is a constant solution x = A; each critical point corresponds to one.

concepts.name: Critical point
concepts.statement: The critical points, or equilibria, of dx/dt = f(x) are the points on the x-axis where f(x) = 0.

concepts.name: Stable critical point
concepts.statement: A critical point is stable if small perturbations of the initial condition do not lead to substantially different solutions as t grows: solutions starting near it tend to it as t → ∞; on the phase diagram both arrows point toward it.

concepts.name: Unstable critical point
concepts.statement: A critical point that is not stable is unstable: on the phase diagram at least one arrow points away from it.

concepts.name: Semistable critical point
concepts.statement: An unstable critical point with one of the arrows of its phase diagram pointing toward it is sometimes called semistable.

concepts.name: Logistic equation
concepts.statement: The logistic equation dx/dt = kx(M − x), for positive k and M, models a population with limiting population M, the maximum sustainable population.

concepts.name: Phase diagram
concepts.statement: The phase diagram, or phase portrait, of an autonomous equation x′ = f(x) is the x-axis drawn vertically with the critical points marked and an arrow between them, up where f(x) > 0 and down where f(x) < 0; it shows the long-term behavior of solutions without solving.

concepts.name: Logistic equation with harvesting
concepts.statement: The logistic equation with harvesting dx/dt = kx(M − x) − h removes h per unit time from a logistic population; its critical points are A and B = (kM ± √((kM)² − 4hk))/2k, two, one or none as h grows.

concepts.name: Euler’s method
concepts.statement: Euler’s method approximates the solution of y′ = f(x, y), y(x₀) = y₀, by following the slope for a step of length h: x_{i+1} = x_i + h and y_{i+1} = y_i + h f(x_i, y_i), the points joined by line segments; y_i approximates y(x_i).

forms.latex: x_{i+1} = x_i + h , \qquad y_{i+1} = y_i + h\, f(x_i,y_i)
forms.ktex: x_{i+1} = x_i + h , \qquad y_{i+1} = y_i + h\, \kf(x_i,y_i)

concepts.name: Step size
concepts.statement: The step size h is the length of the interval on the x-axis followed along one slope in a step of a numerical method.

concepts.name: Error
concepts.statement: The error of an approximation is the size of the difference between the actual solution and the approximate one, |actual y − approximate y|; its sign is not cared about, and it is usually not known exactly.

concepts.name: Order of a numerical method
concepts.statement: A numerical method is of order n if halving the step size multiplies the error by about (1/2)ⁿ: Euler’s method is a first-order method (the error halves), the improved Euler method a second-order method (it quarters) and Runge–Kutta a fourth-order method (it falls by 1/16).

concepts.name: Stiff problem
concepts.statement: A stiff problem is a numerically unstable equation for which the approximations never seem to stabilize as the step size is halved, needing a ridiculously small step.

concepts.name: Runge–Kutta method
concepts.statement: The standard Runge–Kutta method computes four slopes in each step, k₁ = f(x_i, y_i), k₂ = f(x_i + h/2, y_i + k₁h/2), k₃ = f(x_i + h/2, y_i + k₂h/2), k₄ = f(x_i + h, y_i + k₃h), and sets y_{i+1} = y_i + h(k₁ + 2k₂ + 2k₃ + k₄)/6; it is a fourth-order method.

concepts.name: Improved Euler’s method
concepts.statement: The improved Euler method takes the slope k₁ = f(x_i, y_i), the slope k₂ = f(x_i + h, y_i + k₁h) at the point Euler’s step reaches, and steps with their average: y_{i+1} = y_i + h(k₁ + k₂)/2; it is a second-order method.

concepts.name: Potential function
concepts.statement: A potential function is a function F(x, y) of two variables whose curves of constant potential F(x, y) = C are the solutions of an exact equation; the name suggests potential energy or electric potential.

concepts.name: Equipotential curve
concepts.statement: The curves F(x, y) = C of constant potential are sometimes called equipotential curves.

concepts.name: Total derivative
concepts.statement: The total derivative of F(x, y) is dF = F_x dx + F_y dy.

forms.latex: dF = \frac{\partial F}{\partial x} dx + \frac{\partial F}{\partial y} dy

concepts.name: Exact equation
concepts.statement: An equation M dx + N dy = 0, or M + N dy/dx = 0, is exact if it was obtained as dF = 0 for some potential function F, that is M = F_x and N = F_y; the implicit solution is F(x, y) = C.

concepts.name: Vector field
concepts.statement: A vector field assigns to each point (x, y) of the plane a vector, a direction and a magnitude, such as v⃗ = (M, N) with M and N functions of (x, y).

concepts.name: Conservative vector field
concepts.statement: A conservative vector field comes with a potential function F(x, y) such that v⃗ = (∂F/∂x, ∂F/∂y); the work along a path depends only on its endpoints, F(x₂, y₂) − F(x₁, y₁). An exact equation is a conservative vector field.

concepts.name: Solving an exact equation
concepts.statement: Once the equation is known to be exact, integrate F_x = M in x to get F(x, y) = something + A(y), then differentiate this F in y, set it equal to N and find A(y) by integration; F(x, y) = C is the implicit solution. The steps may also be done in the other order.

concepts.name: Test for exactness
concepts.statement: If M = F_x and N = F_y with continuous second derivatives, then M_y = N_x; so if M_y ≠ N_x the equation is not exact.

concepts.name: Poincaré Lemma
concepts.statement: If M and N are continuously differentiable functions of (x, y) and ∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x, then near any point there is a function F(x, y) with M = ∂F/∂x and N = ∂F/∂y; on a region with no holes such an F exists on the whole region.

concepts.name: Integrating factor for an exact equation
concepts.statement: A nonzero u(x, y) makes u M dx + u N dy = 0 exact when (M_y − N_x)u = u_x N − u_y M. If P(x) = (M_y − N_x)/N depends on x alone, u(x) = e^(∫P(x) dx) works; if Q(y) = (M_y − N_x)/M depends on y alone, u(y) = e^(−∫Q(y) dy) works.

concepts.name: First-order linear PDE
concepts.statement: A first-order linear PDE for u(x, t) is a u_x + b u_t + c u = g, with coefficients a, b, c and g functions of x and t (mostly constant or zero here), given with an initial condition u(x, 0) = f(x) for −∞ < x < ∞, t > 0.

forms.latex: a(x,t) \, u_x + b(x,t) \, u_t + c(x,t) \, u = g(x,t), \quad u(x,0) = f(x)

concepts.name: Initial condition for a PDE
concepts.statement: The initial condition u(x, 0) = f(x) of a PDE in x and t is a function of x rather than a number: the equation describes how that function evolves as time goes on.

concepts.name: Method of characteristics
concepts.statement: The method of characteristics finds curves (x(s), t(s)) with dx/ds = a, dt/ds = b, starting at (ξ, 0), along which the PDE a u_x + b u_t + c u = g becomes the linear ODE du/ds + cu = g; it is solved with the initial value f(ξ) and the answer written back in x and t.

concepts.name: Transport equation
concepts.statement: The transport equation is α u_x + u_t = 0 with α a constant: everything travels at the constant speed α.

concepts.name: Solution of the transport equation
concepts.statement: The solution of α u_x + u_t = 0, u(x, 0) = f(x), is u(x, t) = f(x − αt): the initial profile moves to the right with velocity α (to the left if α < 0).

concepts.name: Characteristic coordinates
concepts.statement: Characteristic coordinates (ξ, s) are coordinates in which the PDE simplifies to an ODE in s; for the transport equation they are ξ = x − αt, s = t.

concepts.name: Characteristic curve
concepts.statement: The characteristic curves of a first-order PDE are the curves ξ = constant, along which the data propagate; for the transport equation they are the lines t = (x − ξ)/α of slope 1/α.

concepts.name: Convection
concepts.statement: Convection is the behavior in which everything travels at some constant speed, as in the transport equation: material carried along by a river without diffusing.

concepts.name: ODE along a characteristic
concepts.statement: Along a characteristic curve (x(s), t(s)) with dx/ds = a and dt/ds = b, the chain rule turns a u_x + b u_t + c u = g into the linear ODE du/ds + cu = g in s, with ξ a parameter.
